Could you please tell me in the BH government, was there an agreement about how weapons that had been procured or produced, manufactured in Bosnia and Herzegovina were to be distributed?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell the Trial Chamber at this point that right at the beginning of the war, there was an agreement about humanitarian aid during the war, that humanitarian aid should be divided in three parts. During the war, first the -- in fact, the armed conflict in Central Bosnia broke out because of this shortage of weapons because nobody had enough weapons and the embargo, the arms embargo was in place. In such circumstances, there was an agreement in place. My late deputy confirmed this agreement, Hakija Turajlic because he was in charge of economic relations as I've already indicated. The agreement was to divide the weapons as follows: 50 per cent to the HVO and 50 per cent to the BH army, whenever we could obtain some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me show you, well it will be very easy to go through this document that I have already exhibited, that's 2D 147. In fact, your name is mentioned here. Could you please let me know when you found it?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The 4th Corps Command the date is the 17th of February 1993 and the topic is the manufacture of ammunition and the delivery of this ammunition from Igman Konjic factory -- Igman factory in Konjic, who it was delivered to and so on. For the most part to the 4th Corps or rather all of it was delivered to the 4th corps and to individual brigades. Item 2 on page 2 this is where you are mentioned. Checking with Dzevad Hadjihuseinovic I ascertained that he has a memo from the BH government dated the 31st of January 1993. It does not have a reference number. It is not signed by Mile Akmadzic, but there is a stamp of the BH government where it is indicated that an order issued to distribute all the ammunition that is delivered and manufactured in the ratio of 50/50 between the BH army and the HVO, and it is indicated that this had not been done; and it goes on to say having gone through the information about the ammunition delivered in the period between the 1st of January and the 12th of February 1993 you can see that this order was not complied with and this also pertains to the period that Dzevad mentioned. So do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember the agreement. I don't remember the order because other people had to comply with the order, but we did have this agreement in place and this gentleman, he's obviously referring to that, to this agreement that the weapons and ammunition should be divided in two equal parts. Obviously the armed forces that were dealing with that did not comply with this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this agreement was in place, the date on this document is the 17th of February, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to adhere, I do apologise that we did not have a written agreement to that effect. An agreement that we reached was valid even if we didn't have a written contract or a written agreement. We considered it to be in force.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But to avoid any confusion, in this document, Mr. Dzevad says that he received on the 31st of January, 1993 something that he refers to as an order or rather having checked with Dzevad, I ascertained that he has a memo from the government without your signature about this kind of distribution?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to make this clear, there is a memo and this memo is accurate, but an agreement between the two sides, it's a completely different thing. The memo is also an authentic thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, this is sufficient for my purposes. Could we please look at the next document in the binder 2D 228. These documents are rather brief, and we'll deal with them briefly. This is a document from the command of the 4th Corps, the date is -- the date precedes the one from the previous document and you indicated that at that time an agreement was in place. It is signed by Mr. Arif Pasalic and in the first part he says, I order hereby that at all the checkpoints controlled by the BH army and the military police, the checks of persons and vehicles should be stepped up and also of any cargo being transported and in relation to this, any attempts to transport weapons, mines or explosives and personnel for the purposes of the HVO should be prevented. Mr. Akmadzic, you saw this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To your knowledge, how -- what's the amount of weapons and ammunition that arrived and was delivered to the BH army? I'm not asking you about the exact figures but how many weapons arrived, reached the BH army through HVO-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: MILE AKMADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army could obtain weapons in one of the two ways: Weapons were manufactured in defence industry plants in Central Bosnia and in Igman Konjic Plant and the other source is weapons that had to be transported through HVO-controlled territory. Now as to the quantities of those weapons it is difficult for me to say that, but all weapons that the BH army obtained was obtained in these two ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much Your Honours, I have a very brief document that I want to go through, if we can go through this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a follow-up question. For an external observer this situation seems paradoxical, surprising, amazing. These documents were shown to other witnesses and it seems that the BH army received weapons via the HVO. At the same time, the BH army was engaged in military action against the HVO. So what kind of explanation could you proffer about the situation which seems really astonishing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are situations that were even more paradoxical, situations that I did not mention. Well, the third source available to them was buying weapons from Republika Srpska. There are so many paradoxical situations in this war but the BH army and the HVO never ceased being partners. There was always some kind of an agreement in place regardless of the fighting that was going on. I myself attended a meeting or a conversation with Mr. Boban. At that time, I was not the prime minister, but Mr. Boban was asked to deliver a certain quantity of weapons, and he promised that he would do so in my presence. I didn't follow up on this, I can tell you now who asked for it but I don't think this is relevant for the present case. So in particular in the first stage of the fighting of the war when the production plants were not running at full capacity and when the technology was not there, the know-how was not there, most of the weapons the BH army obtained it obtained through or from the HVO. Mr. Izetbegovic himself told me that even the town of Sarajevo which was under siege received certain quantities of weapons and since we were on good terms, I asked him how, when it is impossible for a bird to fly into the town itself, and he told me: Mile, it's possible to transport weapons on horseback. Now, whether there were some other channels such as for instance bringing in weapons with the humanitarian relief supplies, well I cannot testify about that because sanctions were in place, and I don't know about that. But it is quite possible that there were such instances. I'm talking about air transport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are forced to stop now. Yesterday, we went extra time. So Witness, we will resume tomorrow at quarter past 2.00. You probably understood that you will probably have to be here on Monday since we're not able to finish with the Defence questions. Ms. Nozica, you have used up 1 hour and 11 minutes. Tomorrow, the Defence will finish cross-examination and then the Prosecution will start its cross-examination. So you will have to be here until Monday afternoon, unfortunately. We could not do anything about it. We will resume tomorrow at quarter past 2.00. I wish you nice evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of June, 2008 at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
